teaser.text: BOC Hong Kong (Holdings) Limited is a banking group that looks after money, finances borrowing and helps customers pay, invest and insure. Its main operating bank, Bank of China (Hong Kong), or BOCHK, earns through both interest-bearing finance and services that charge fees or trading spreads.

stock.title: BOCHK stock forecast
stock.meta_description: BOCHK stock forecast: weighted prices, bear, base and bull drivers, dividends, earnings and valuation in plain English.
stock.opening: The weighted scenario puts BOCHK at HK$48.31 in October 2027, including dividends. It hinges on loan growth supporting net interest income, lower credit costs without large write-offs, and recurring fees from private banking and cross-border services.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains BOCHK’s business, its rivals, its management and its risks.

paragraphs.text: The forecast gives BOCHK a weighted price of HK$48.31 in October 2027, HK$49.01 in October 2028 and HK$50.54 in October 2029, including dividends. Against today’s HK$50.45, those outcomes represent approximately 0%, 5% and 13% returns.

The 2029 range is wide: HK$31.41 in the bear case to HK$75.94 in the bull case. The base case remains the central outcome because capital, earnings and dividends continue to grow, but continued margin pressure limits expected rerating.

blocks.heading: What has to go right, and what could go wrong for BOCHK?

paragraphs.text: The bear case requires prolonged NIM pressure, weak loan demand and larger property or mainland credit losses. Earnings weaken, dividends fall and investors reduce the premium paid for BOCHK’s book value. The price falls from HK$37.29 in October 2027 to HK$31.41 in October 2029. Its 28% probability reflects real credit and margin risks, but also the bank’s capital buffer and absence of evidence for forced dilution.

The bull case requires stronger loan growth, disciplined deposit pricing, lower credit costs without heavy write-offs, and recurring wealth and cross-border fee growth. Capital generation then supports higher dividends and buybacks, while durable ROE supports a rising P/B multiple. The price reaches HK$58.77 in October 2027 and HK$75.94 in October 2029. Its 17% probability is lower because buybacks are discretionary and the improvements must occur together.

blocks.heading: What does BOCHK earn and give back?

paragraphs.text: A dividend transfers cash to shareholders and reduces retained capital. BOCHK’s implied payout rose between 2021 and 2025. Management’s regular payout range is 40%–60%, and its 2026–2028 programme targets at least HK$10.5 billion of additional shareholder returns.

dividend.title: BOCHK dividend: payout, coverage and yield
dividend.meta_description: BOCHK dividend history, cash coverage, payout plans and current yield, with the main risks that could change distributions.
dividend.opening: BOCHK pays a regular dividend, with payout guided at 40%–60% of earnings, while distributions compete with retained capital and future credit losses. The memo shows dividends, buybacks and capital kept to grow and build capital rather than a simple free-cash-flow cover test.
dividend.closing: The full BOCHK memo also covers its business, rivals, management decisions and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does BOCHK pay in dividends per share?

paragraphs.text: For a bank, retained earnings are not simply cash left in a drawer. They become equity that can support new loans and investments, absorb losses or remain as a safety cushion. BOCHK’s common earnings rose over the five years, and its common-dividend payout ratio also increased. The share count stayed unchanged, so the earnings improvement was spread across the same number of shares.

paragraphs.text: Base paid DPS is HK$2.00 in October 2027. It rises to HK$2.25 in October 2028 and HK$2.40 in October 2029. The path reflects rising earnings and a payout within management’s 40%–60% target. The bear case gives HK$1.80, HK$1.60 and HK$1.50 as margin and credit pressure restrain distributions. The bull case gives HK$2.20, HK$2.65 and HK$3.00 as earnings and payouts improve. The already-paid special dividend is not counted again.
